ModMetaData.name: Adaptive Storage Neolithic Renew
ModMetaData.author: Soul, Phaneron, bradson - 1.6 port: nelim
ModMetaData.description:
Tribal storage for the Adaptive Storage Framework: baskets of wood, leather and fabric, large pots for raw food, stacked stone chunks, wood and hay piles, a meal shelf, textile and leather bundles, and carved plinths for displaying a single item.
Every container shows what is inside it. Fill a basket and you see the basket fill up.
Two neolithic research projects unlock the set, both available from a tribal start.
REQUIRES the Adaptive Storage Framework. It does nothing on its own.
I am not the author of this mod. The buildings, their artwork and their stats are Soul's, Phaneron's and bradson's - all I did was bring the module forward to 1.6. Credit goes to them; mistakes in the port are mine.
Original mod: https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3033901895 - declares 1.4 and 1.5 and nothing further.
WHAT CHANGED
Almost nothing, and that is the honest answer. Three quarters of this mod is declarative graphics carried by the framework, and the framework itself already supports 1.6. Every XML element in the mod still maps to a field that exists in 1.6, and every C# type it names is still present in the framework's 1.6 assemblies. Nothing had to be rewritten.
Two faults were fixed on the way through.
The Russian translation lived in a folder spelled "Definjected". RimWorld looks for the exact string "DefInjected", so on Windows it worked by accident and on Linux - the Steam Deck included - the whole Russian translation was silently dropped. The folder is now spelled correctly.
1.6 added a sixth kind of stone chunk, vacstone, with the Odyssey expansion. The mod builds a large pot, a plinth and a chunk stack out of every stone chunk in the game, so it picks vacstone up automatically - but the French translation was written when there were five, and the vacstone pieces came out untranslated. French now covers all six. Russian still covers five; I do not write Russian, and rather than invent it I left it to a Russian speaker.
Unused files that shipped with the original are not published here: a shelved folder of textures the mod never loads, and a duplicate .dds copy of the Workshop preview image that nothing reads. They are kept in the repository, out of the published folder.
The buildings themselves - their stats, their costs, their graphics - are untouched.
CREDIT AND LICENCE
This mod is MIT licensed by its authors, and the LICENSE file travels with it, here and in the repository. That is a written permission, not an assumption: unlike most ports, this one did not need anybody's silence.
The original defNames are kept, so a save moves between the two mods without losing anything. The two cannot run together - the original is declared incompatible above. Run one or the other.
Content mod: removing it mid-save destroys any of these containers already built, and drops what was inside them.
Source, changelog and attribution: https://github.com/vbardales/Rimworld-Adaptive-Storage-Neolithic-Renew
The port work was done with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, by Anthropic), and the mod icon and the preview image were generated with an image model, under human direction. Those two images are the only things here that are not the authors' own: the artwork you see in game is entirely theirs. Thanks to Soul, Phaneron and bradson for the mod and for licensing it openly, and to Elzetia for the French translation this port extends.
If I do not answer within a reasonable time after being contacted, anyone may freely update this or any other of my mods, including publishing a continuation of it. All credit must be preserved.
